gloss: be firm, sure; be faithful; believe, trust; truth; amen
summary: To be firm and sure, so that one can lean on it: a peg in a sure place, waters that do not fail, a house made sure, a word confirmed. Of people and of God the niphal is to be faithful, one who can be relied on; the hiphil is to rely on another, to believe and trust, as Abraham believed Yahweh and it was counted to him as righteousness. The nouns are אֱמֶת, firmness, faithfulness and truth, what holds and is so, often beside חֶסֶד; אֱמוּנָה, steadiness and faithfulness, by which the righteous will live; and אָמֵן, “firm, so be it”, the people's answer that confirms a word, carried into the New Testament as ἀμήν. The qal is to carry and foster a child, and a few words name a craftsman, whose tie to the root's sense is not clear.

words.gloss: (qal) foster, carry; (niphal) be firm, sure, confirmed, faithful; (hiphil) believe, trust
words.summary: About 110 times. The niphal and hiphil carry the root's sense: what is firm can be leaned on (niphal), and to lean on it is to believe or trust (hiphil). Isa 7:9 sets the two side by side: “if you do not believe (תַאֲמִינוּ), you will not be made firm (תֵאָמֵנוּ)”. The qal, to carry and foster a child, is a sense apart; its tie to firmness (one who holds up and supports the child) is not shown by the text or by any cognate. Isa 30:21 תַאֲמִינוּ, filed here by spelling, is the verb “go to the right” (ימנ). The brief's tokens with no stem are the passive participle (2Sa 20:19), the noun אֵמֻן (Psa 12:2 and others, counted under both keys), and אֹמְנוֹת “supports” (2Ki 18:16), entered as its own word.

stems.gloss: carry, foster, nurse (a child); (passive) reared; faithful

senses.gloss: carry and foster a child; a nurse, guardian
senses.definition: The active participle: one who carries, brings up and keeps a child not his own, a nurse or foster-father, or the guardians of a king's sons.

evidence.note: “Carry him in your bosom as הָאֹמֵן carries the suckling.”
Naomi laid the child in her bosom “and became his לְאֹמֶנֶת”.
Mordecai “was אֹמֵן Hadassah … for she had no father or mother”: bringing her up as a daughter.
Mephibosheth's nurse (אֹמַנְתּוֹ) took him up and fled.
Jehu wrote to “the guardians (הָאֹמְנִים) of Ahab's sons”.
“Kings will be אֹמְנַיִךְ, and their princesses your nursing mothers (מֵינִיקֹתַיִךְ).”

senses.definition: The passive participle of children carried and brought up.

evidence.note: “Those הָאֱמֻנִים on scarlet embrace dunghills.”

senses.definition: The passive participle as a noun: those who are firm and faithful, who keep faith.

evidence.note: “I am of the peaceable and אֱמוּנֵי of Israel.”

stems.gloss: be firm, lasting, sure; be confirmed; be faithful, trustworthy; be carried

senses.definition: Of things: to be firm and lasting, so that they can be relied on and do not fail; a place that holds a peg, waters that do not run dry, a house and a kingdom that stand.

evidence.note: “I will fasten him as a peg בְּמָקוֹם נֶאֱמָן.”
“The peg fastened בְּמָקוֹם נֶאֱמָן shall give way.”
“His bread is given, his waters נֶאֱמָנִים”: sure, not failing.
“Will you be to me like a deceptive brook (אַכְזָב), waters לֹא נֶאֱמָנוּ?”: the opposite, the wadi that runs dry.
Plagues “great and נֶאֱמָנוֹת”: lasting, that do not go away.
“Your house and your kingdom וְנֶאְמַן before you forever; your throne shall be established (נָכוֹן) forever.”
“I will build him בַּיִת נֶאֱמָן.”
“Yahweh will certainly make my lord בַּיִת נֶאֱמָן.”
“My covenant shall stand fast (נֶאֱמֶנֶת) with him.”
“Your testimonies are very sure.”
“The testimony of Yahweh is sure, making wise the simple.”
“All his precepts are sure.”
Among the tribes of Israel “I make known נֶאֱמָנָה”: what is sure.
“An everlasting covenant, the kindnesses of David הַנֶּאֱמָנִים”: quoted in Act 13:34 of the resurrection.
“I will give you the holy things of David, the sure ones (τὰ πιστά)”: Isa 55:3, said of raising Jesus from the dead.

senses.definition: Of words and promises: to be shown to be firm, borne out by the event.

evidence.note: “Bring your youngest brother to me, וְיֵאָמְנוּ דִבְרֵיכֶם, and you shall not die.”
“Let your word, I pray, יֵאָמֶן, which you spoke to your servant David.”

senses.definition: Of people and of God: one who can be relied on, who keeps his word and his charge.

evidence.note: “Not so my servant Moses: in all my house נֶאֱמָן הוּא”; quoted in Heb 3:2, 5.
“Yahweh your God, he is God, הָאֵל הַנֶּאֱמָן, keeping the covenant and the kindness to those who love him.”
“Because of Yahweh who is faithful (נֶאֱמָן), the Holy One of Israel, who has chosen you.”
“You found his heart נֶאֱמָן before you, and made with him the covenant.”
“Who among all your servants is as faithful as David?”
All Israel knew that Samuel “was established (נֶאֱמָן) as a prophet of Yahweh”: attested, proved trustworthy.
“How the קִרְיָה נֶאֱמָנָה has become a harlot! She was full of justice.”
“I took to me עֵדִים נֶאֱמָנִים to witness.”
“Yahweh be a true (אֱמֶת) and faithful (נֶאֱמָן) witness against us.”
David's seed established forever as the moon, “a witness in the sky, נֶאֱמָן”.
“A generation that did not set its heart right, and whose spirit was not נֶאֶמְנָה with God.”
“My eyes shall be on the faithful of the land.”
“A slanderer reveals a secret, but נֶאֱמַן־רוּחַ covers a matter.”
“A faithful messenger to those who send him.”
“נֶאֱמָנִים are the wounds of a friend.”
Treasurers appointed “for they were counted faithful”.
He removes the speech “of the trusted (נֶאֱמָנִים)”.
Jesus “faithful to him who appointed him, as also Moses in all his house”: Num 12:7.

senses.definition: In Isa 7:9 and 2Ch 20:20, set beside the hiphil: to be held firm, to stand, as the result of believing.

evidence.note: “If you do not believe (תַאֲמִינוּ), you will not be made firm (תֵאָמֵנוּ).”
“Believe (הַאֲמִינוּ) in Yahweh your God and you will be made firm (וְתֵאָמֵנוּ).”

senses.definition: The passive of the qal: to be carried by a nurse.

evidence.note: “Your daughters on the side תֵּאָמַנָה”: carried as by a nurse, as Isa 49:23's kings fostering Zion.

senses.gloss: believe, trust (in a person, God, a word)
senses.definition: To lean on another as firm: to take his word as sure and act on it, to trust him; with בְּ of the one trusted or ל of the one or the word believed. Its opposite is to refuse to listen and to rebel.

evidence.note: “וְהֶאֱמִן in Yahweh, and he counted it to him as righteousness”: Abraham believed the promise of a seed (Gen 15:5); quoted in Rom 4:3; Gal 3:6; Jas 2:23.
“They will not believe me or listen to my voice.”
“If they will not believe you, nor listen to the voice of the first sign, they will believe the voice of the latter sign.”
“And the people believed, and they heard that Yahweh had visited the sons of Israel.”
“The people feared Yahweh, וַיַּאֲמִינוּ in Yahweh and in Moses his servant.”
“That the people may hear when I speak with you, and believe you forever.”
“How long will they not believe in me, for all the signs I have done among them?”
Moses and Aaron: “because you did not believe in me, to treat me as holy.”
“Yet in this thing you did not believe Yahweh your God.”
“You rebelled against the mouth of Yahweh your God, and did not believe him, nor listen to his voice.”
“They hardened their neck … who did not believe in Yahweh their God.”
“Because they did not believe in God, and did not trust (בָטְחוּ) in his salvation.”
“Then they believed his words; they sang his praise.”
“They despised the pleasant land; they did not believe his word.”
“I believed, for I will speak”: quoted in 2Co 4:13.
“I believe in your commandments.”
“Unless I had believed to see the goodness of Yahweh in the land of the living.”
“Behold, I lay in Zion a stone … הַמַּאֲמִין will not hasten”; quoted in Rom 9:33; 10:11; 1Pe 2:6 of Christ.
“That you may know וְתַאֲמִינוּ לִי and understand that I am he.”
“Who has believed our report?”; quoted in Jhn 12:38; Rom 10:16.
“A work you will not believe, though it be told you”; quoted in Act 13:41.
“The men of Nineveh believed God”, and proclaimed a fast.
“Believe in Yahweh your God … believe his prophets, and prosper.”
“Abraham believed (ἐπίστευσεν) God, and it was counted to him for righteousness”: Gen 15:6.

senses.definition: To take a report or a word as true.

evidence.note: Told that Joseph was alive, Jacob's heart went numb, “for he did not believe them”.
“I did not believe the words until I came and my eyes had seen.”
“The simple believes every word, but the prudent considers his steps.”
“When he speaks graciously, do not believe him.”
“Do not believe them, though they speak good words to you.”
Gedaliah “did not believe them”.
The kings of the earth did not believe that the enemy would enter Jerusalem's gates.
“Do not believe him.”

senses.gloss: trust, rely on (a person, an animal)
senses.definition: To trust someone with a charge, or to count on someone or something.

evidence.note: “Achish trusted (וַיַּאֲמֵן) David, saying, He has made himself odious to his people.”
“Sihon did not trust Israel to pass through his border.”
“Do not trust in a friend; do not rely (תִּבְטְחוּ) on a companion.”
“He does not trust in his servants.”
“Let him not trust in emptiness.”
“Will you trust the wild ox to bring home your seed?”
“I smiled at them, they did not believe it.”

senses.definition: With a negative and “life”: to have no assurance of living.

evidence.note: “You will fear night and day, וְלֹא תַאֲמִין בְּחַיֶּיךָ.”
“He rises up, and no one is sure of life.”
“He does not believe that he will return out of darkness.”

senses.definition: Of the war horse at the trumpet: it does not stand firm, cannot hold still; or does not believe that it is the trumpet.

evidence.note: “With fierceness and rage he swallows the ground, וְלֹא־יַאֲמִין that it is the sound of the trumpet.”

evidence.locator: Gen.15.6, הֶאֱמִן → ἐπίστευσεν; Isa.28.16, הַמַּאֲמִין → ὁ πιστεύων; Isa.53.1 → ἐπίστευσεν; Hab.1.5 → πιστεύσητε; Psa.116.10 → ἐπίστευσα

evidence.note: Gen 15:6: “Abraham believed God.”
Isa 28:16: “Whoever believes on him will not be put to shame.”
Isa 53:1: “Lord, who has believed our report?”
Hab 1:5: “a work which you will not believe.”
Psa 116:10: “I believed, therefore I spoke.”

evidence.locator: Num.12.7, נֶאֱמָן → πιστός; Deu.7.9 → πιστός; Isa.55.3, הַנֶּאֱמָנִים → τὰ πιστά

evidence.note: Num 12:7: “faithful … as Moses in all his house.”
Isa 55:3: “the sure (τὰ πιστά) holy things of David.”
“God is faithful”, as Deu 7:9.

parallels.note: “Listen to the voice”: to believe is to heed.
“Be established”: beside the niphal of a house and kingdom.

opposites.note: “A deceptive brook”, waters that fail, against waters that are sure.
“Rebel”: not believing is rebelling against his mouth.

phrases.gloss: a sure house, a lasting line

words.summary: About 127 times, contracted from *ʾamint. It is what is firm: faithfulness that holds to its word (often with חֶסֶד, kindness and faithfulness), and truth, the word or matter that holds because it is so. After a noun it says “true, sure”: a true sign, a sure reward, true judgment.

senses.definition: Constancy that keeps faith: God's or a man's holding to what he has promised and to those he is bound to, often joined with חֶסֶד.

evidence.note: “Who has not forsaken his kindness וַאֲמִתּוֹ toward my master.”
“Yahweh, Yahweh, a God merciful and gracious … abundant in kindness וֶאֱמֶת.” Compare Jhn 1:14, “full of grace and truth”.
“If you will deal kindly וֶאֱמֶת with my master, tell me.”
“I am not worthy of all the kindnesses and all the faithfulness you have shown your servant.”
“Deal with me in kindness וֶאֱמֶת: do not bury me in Egypt.”
“You will give אֱמֶת to Jacob, kindness to Abraham, which you swore to our fathers.”
“All the paths of Yahweh are kindness וֶאֱמֶת to those who keep his covenant.”
“Kindness and truth have met; righteousness and peace have kissed.”
“His faithfulness is a shield and buckler.”
“The faithfulness of Yahweh endures forever.”
“Who keeps אֱמֶת forever.”
“Will the dust praise you? Will it declare your faithfulness?”
“Those who go down to the pit do not hope for your faithfulness.”
“The father to the children shall make known your faithfulness.”
“Let not kindness and truth forsake you; bind them on your neck.”
“By kindness and truth iniquity is covered.”
“There is no אֱמֶת, no kindness, no knowledge of God in the land.”
“You have acted faithfully (אֱמֶת), but we have done wickedly.”
“I will plant them in this land בֶּאֱמֶת, with all my heart.”
“I will be their God, בֶּאֱמֶת and in righteousness.”

senses.gloss: faithfulness, sincerity (of a man's walk and service)
senses.definition: A whole-hearted and constant walk with God or dealing with men, without pretence.

evidence.note: “Fear Yahweh and serve him in wholeness (בְּתָמִים) וּבֶאֱמֶת; put away the gods.”
“To walk before me בֶּאֱמֶת with all their heart and all their soul.”
Hezekiah: “I have walked before you בֶּאֱמֶת and with a whole heart.”
“Yahweh is near to all who call on him in truth.”
“They will lean on Yahweh, the Holy One of Israel, בֶּאֱמֶת.”
They swear by the name of Yahweh “not in truth and not in righteousness”.
“If you swear, As Yahweh lives, בֶּאֱמֶת, in justice and righteousness.”
“If you have acted בֶּאֱמֶת and wholeness in making Abimelech king.”
“Men of ability, fearing God, אַנְשֵׁי אֱמֶת, hating unjust gain.”
Hananiah “was a man of faithfulness (אִישׁ אֱמֶת) and feared God above many”.

senses.gloss: truth: what is so; a true word
senses.definition: Of a report, a word or a judgment: that it holds, that it is so; the truth spoken, as against lies and deceit. Of God's word and law: the truth.

evidence.note: “If this thing is אֱמֶת, and the tokens of virginity were not found.”
“Inquire diligently, and behold, אֱמֶת, the thing is certain (נָכוֹן).”
“That your words may be proved, whether אֱמֶת is in you.”
“אֱמֶת was the report I heard in my own land.”
“Now I know that you are a man of God, and the word of Yahweh in your mouth is אֱמֶת.”
“Speak to me nothing but אֱמֶת in the name of Yahweh.”
“They deceive each his neighbour, and do not speak אֱמֶת; they have taught their tongue to speak lies (שֶׁקֶר).”
“Speak אֱמֶת each with his neighbour”; quoted in Eph 4:25.
“Love אֱמֶת and peace.”
“Jerusalem shall be called the city of truth (עִיר־הָאֱמֶת).”
“Judge מִשְׁפַּט אֱמֶת.”
He “executes מִשְׁפַּט אֱמֶת between man and man”.
“He speaks truth in his heart.”
“You desire truth in the inward parts.”
Wisdom: “My mouth will speak אֱמֶת; wickedness is an abomination to my lips.”
“The lip of אֱמֶת shall be established forever, but a lying tongue is but for a moment.”
“A true witness (עֵד אֱמֶת) delivers lives.”
“Buy truth, and do not sell it.”
“Words of truth, written uprightly.”
“He who has my word, let him speak my word אֱמֶת.”
The prophet of peace is known “when the word of the prophet comes to pass … that Yahweh has truly (בֶּאֱמֶת) sent him”.
“Let them hear and say, It is אֱמֶת.”
“Truth has stumbled in the street.”
“I will give their reward בֶּאֱמֶת.”
“He will bring forth justice לֶאֱמֶת”: so that it holds.
The horn “cast truth to the ground”.
“The vision of the evening and the morning … is אֱמֶת.”
“The word was אֱמֶת.”
“What is inscribed in the writing of truth (בִּכְתָב אֱמֶת).”
“That we might turn from our iniquities and understand your truth.”
“You are God, and your words are אֱמֶת, and you have promised this good thing.”
“The judgments of Yahweh are אֱמֶת, righteous altogether.”
“Do not take the word of truth out of my mouth.”
“Your law is אֱמֶת.” Compare Jhn 17:17, “your word is truth”.
“The head of your word is אֱמֶת.”
“Laws of truth, good statutes and commandments.”
“The law of truth was in his mouth.”
“Lead me in your truth and teach me.”
“Send out your light and your truth; let them lead me.”
“Teach me your way, Yahweh; I will walk in your truth.”
“The works of his hands are אֱמֶת and justice.”
“Words of peace and truth.”
“Your word is truth”, as Psa 119:142, 160.

senses.gloss: true, sure (after a noun); the true God
senses.definition: As the second of two nouns: genuine, to be relied on. Of God, the true God, against the idols.

evidence.note: “Yahweh is the true God (אֱלֹהִים אֱמֶת); he is the living God and an everlasting king”, against the idols of 10:1–9.
“For a long time Israel was without a true God.”
“You have redeemed me, Yahweh, God of truth.”
“Give me אוֹת אֱמֶת”: a sure sign.
“He who sows righteousness, a reward of אֱמֶת”: a sure reward.
“I planted you a choice vine, wholly זֶרַע אֱמֶת”: a true, sound seed.
“I will give you שְׁלוֹם אֱמֶת in this place”: assured peace, the false prophets' word.
“Abundance of peace וֶאֱמֶת.”
“Will there not be peace וֶאֱמֶת in my days?”: lasting peace.
“A true and faithful witness.”
“Yahweh has sworn אֱמֶת to David; he will not turn from it.”

evidence.locator: Psa.119.142, אֱמֶת → ἀλήθεια; Zec.8.16 → ἀλήθειαν; ἀλήθεια renders אֱמֶת ×59

evidence.note: Zec 8:16: “Speak truth each with his neighbour.”
“Your word is truth”, as Psa 119:142.
“Full of grace and truth”, as Exo 34:6's חֶסֶד וֶאֱמֶת.

evidence.note: “To serve a living and true God”, as Jer 10:10.

“Peace”: peace and truth, peace that lasts.
“Wholeness, integrity”: serving in wholeness and truth.
“Certain, established”: the thing is true and certain.

opposites.note: “Lie, falsehood”: the lip of truth against a lying tongue.
“Deceit”: a true witness against one who breathes out lies.

phrases.gloss: a man of faithfulness, a trustworthy man

words.summary: About 49 times: the quality of being firm. Of Moses' hands, held steady; of men in office, dealing faithfully; above all of Yahweh, whose faithfulness the psalms praise; and in Hab 2:4 the steadfast trust by which the righteous will live, which the New Testament reads as faith.

senses.definition: Of the body and of times: steady, holding firm, not giving way.

evidence.note: Aaron and Hur held up Moses' hands, “and his hands were אֱמוּנָה until the going down of the sun”.
“He will be the stability (אֱמוּנַת) of your times.”

senses.definition: Faithful dealing, especially in a charge or office: honesty that can be trusted without checking.

evidence.note: “They did not reckon with the men into whose hand they gave the silver … for they dealt בֶאֱמֻנָה.”
The gatekeepers whom David and Samuel “ordained in their faithfulness”.
“Thus you shall do in the fear of Yahweh, בֶּאֱמוּנָה and with a whole heart.”
“Yahweh will repay each man his righteousness and his faithfulness.”
“He who breathes out אֱמוּנָה declares righteousness, but a false witness, deceit.”
“Lying lips are an abomination to Yahweh, but those who deal faithfully (עֹשֵׂי אֱמוּנָה) are his delight.”
“A man of faithfulness (אִישׁ אֱמוּנוֹת) will abound with blessings.”
“If you can find a man, if there is one who does justice, who seeks אֱמוּנָה, and I will pardon her.”
“אֱמוּנָה has perished, and is cut off from their mouth.”
“They bend their tongue, their bow, for lies, and not for faithfulness.”
“No one sues in righteousness, and no one pleads בֶּאֱמוּנָה.”
“Dwell in the land and feed on faithfulness.”
“I have chosen the way of faithfulness.”
Of the shoot of Jesse: “righteousness the belt of his loins, and וְהָאֱמוּנָה the belt of his waist.”

senses.definition: Yahweh's constancy to his word and covenant, which the psalms praise and lay hold of in prayer.

evidence.note: “The Rock, his work is perfect … אֵל אֱמוּנָה and without iniquity, righteous and upright is he.”
“His mercies are new every morning; great is your faithfulness.”
“With my mouth I will make known your faithfulness to all generations.”
Of David: “My faithfulness and my kindness shall be with him.”
“I will not take my kindness from him, nor be false (אֲשַׁקֵּר) to my faithfulness.”
“The word of Yahweh is upright, and all his work is done in faithfulness.”
“Shall your faithfulness be declared in destruction?”
“He will judge the peoples with his faithfulness.”
“All your commandments are faithfulness.”
“Counsels of old, faithfulness, sureness (אֱמוּנָה אֹמֶן).”
“I will betroth you to me בֶּאֱמוּנָה, and you shall know Yahweh.”

senses.definition: In Hab 2:4, the firmness of the righteous man who holds to the vision and waits for it, against the proud: the trust by which he lives, as the hiphil of the root is to believe.

evidence.note: “Behold, his soul is puffed up, it is not upright in him; but the righteous will live בֶּאֱמוּנָתוֹ”, after “though it tarry, wait for it; for it will surely come” (2:3).

Hab 2:3–4, of waiting for him who is coming.

evidence.locator: Hab.2.4, בֶּאֱמוּנָתוֹ → ἐκ πίστεώς; πίστις renders אֱמוּנָה ×16

evidence.note: Hab 2:4.

parallels.note: “Kindness”: the psalms' pair for God's covenant love.

opposites.note: “Lie”: lying lips against those who deal faithfully.

words.summary: About 30 times: “firm, sure”, said in answer to confirm what another has said, to take a curse or an oath on oneself, to agree to a word, or to close a blessing of Yahweh. In Isa 65:16 Yahweh is “the God of amen”. Borrowed into Greek, ἀμήν, it opens Jesus' sayings and is the name of Christ in Rev 3:14.

senses.gloss: so be it: the answer that confirms a word
senses.definition: Said by the hearer to make another's word his own: accepting a curse or an oath, agreeing to a command or a promise.

evidence.note: The woman under the oath of jealousy “shall say, אָמֵן אָמֵן”: she takes the curse on herself if guilty.
“Cursed is the man who makes a carved image … and all the people shall answer and say, אָמֵן.”
To the oath to restore what was taken: “all the assembly said, אָמֵן, and praised Yahweh, and the people did according to this promise.”
Benaiah to David's word: “אָמֵן; so may Yahweh, the God of my lord the king, say.”
To the covenant and its oath: “Then I answered and said, אָמֵן, Yahweh.”

doctrine.statement: Yahweh brought Abraham outside and said, “Look toward the heavens and count the stars … so shall your seed be”, and “he believed (וְהֶאֱמִן) in Yahweh, and he counted it to him as righteousness” (Gen 15:5–6). What Abraham believed was a promise: a seed from his own body when he had none (Gen 15:4). Paul quotes the verse to show that righteousness was counted to Abraham before circumcision and apart from works of law (Rom 4:3, 9–10), and explains the faith: “being fully persuaded that what he had promised he was able also to perform; therefore it was counted to him for righteousness … not for his sake alone, but for ours also, to whom it will be counted, who believe on him who raised Jesus our Lord from the dead” (Rom 4:21–24). The promise is the gospel preached beforehand to Abraham, and those of faith are blessed with him (Gal 3:6–9). James quotes the same verse of the faith that offered Isaac: “faith worked with his works, and by works faith was made complete” (Jas 2:21–23). From the verses: to believe is to take God's promise as firm and rest one's life on it, as the root's own sense says; Abraham's trust in the promised seed, Christ, was counted as righteousness, and the same trust, shown in obedience, is counted to those who believe God raised Jesus.

Habakkuk is told to write the vision plainly, “for the vision is yet for the appointed time … though it tarry, wait for it; for it will surely come”, and then, “behold, his soul is puffed up, it is not upright in him; but the righteous will live by his אֱמוּנָה” (Hab 2:2–4). The word is the firmness of one who holds to what Yahweh has said and waits for it. Paul quotes it for the gospel, in which “the righteousness of God is revealed from faith to faith” (Rom 1:17), and to show that no one is made righteous by the law (Gal 3:11); Hebrews quotes it with the coming of Christ, “yet a little while, and he who comes will come and will not tarry; but the righteous shall live by faith” (Heb 10:37–38). From the verses: the life promised to the righteous is held by steadfast trust in God's word while the fulfilment waits, and that trust looks to the coming of Christ.

Yahweh promised David, “your house and your kingdom shall be made sure (וְנֶאְמַן) forever before you; your throne shall be established forever” (2Sa 7:16), and the psalm says, “my covenant shall stand fast (נֶאֱמֶנֶת) with him … his seed shall endure forever, and his throne as the sun … as the moon, a faithful (נֶאֱמָן) witness in the sky” (Psa 89:29, 37–38). Isaiah offers an everlasting covenant, “the sure kindnesses of David (חַסְדֵי דָוִד הַנֶּאֱמָנִים)” (Isa 55:3). Paul says God fulfilled the promise “in that he raised up Jesus”, and of raising him from the dead, “no more to return to corruption, he has said thus: I will give you the sure holy things of David” (Act 13:33–34). From the verses: the promise to David is made sure in a son of David who does not die; the resurrection of Jesus is God's faithfulness to that covenant, and the throne it promises is still to be set up.

To Ahaz, faced with the kings of Syria and Israel, Isaiah said, “if you do not believe (תַאֲמִינוּ), you will not be made firm (תֵאָמֵנוּ)” (Isa 7:9); Jehoshaphat said the same to Judah before battle, “believe in Yahweh your God and you shall be made firm” (2Ch 20:20). Yahweh lays in Zion “a tested stone, a precious corner stone of sure foundation; whoever believes will not hasten” (Isa 28:16), and Paul and Peter apply the stone to Christ: “whoever believes on him will not be ashamed” (Rom 9:33; 10:11; 1Pe 2:6). From the verses: firmness comes from leaning on what Yahweh has made firm; the man who believes is made to stand because what he rests on, the stone God has laid, does not give way.

The people said אָמֵן to make a word their own (Num 5:22; Deu 27:15–26), and Yahweh is “the God of amen”, by whom his people will bless themselves and swear (Isa 65:16). The New Testament calls Christ by the same word: “all the promises of God in him are yes, and in him amen” (2Co 1:20), and “these things says the Amen, the faithful and true witness, the beginning of the creation of God” (Rev 3:14). The same book calls him “the faithful witness, the firstborn from the dead” (Rev 1:5), and Paul calls him “the beginning, the firstborn from the dead” (Col 1:18) and says that “if anyone is in Christ, he is a new creation” (2Co 5:17). From the verses: Jesus is the Amen as the one in whom God's promises are confirmed and made sure; he is the beginning of God's creation as the first raised from the dead to immortal life, the head of the new creation.

In Proverbs 8 Wisdom speaks as a woman calling in the streets (Pro 8:1–3; compare 9:1–3): “Yahweh possessed me at the beginning of his way … when he established the heavens, I was there … then I was beside him as an אָמוֹן, and I was his delight day by day” (Pro 8:22, 27, 30). The same book says plainly, “Yahweh by wisdom founded the earth; by understanding he established the heavens” (Pro 3:19). The New Testament says Christ is “the wisdom of God” and “became to us wisdom from God” (1Co 1:24, 30), and of Jesus as a child that he “grew and became strong, filled with wisdom”, and “increased in wisdom and stature” (Luk 2:40, 52). From the verses: Wisdom in Proverbs 8 is God's own wisdom, by which he made the world, spoken of as a person; it is not a second being existing beside God. That wisdom was shown in Jesus, a man who grew in it, and who became to believers the wisdom of God.

note: Drafted 2026-11-18. Root key אמנ, the corpus's and BDB's (a.dy.aa as the root heading). BDB keys assigned: a.dy.aa verb, a.dy.ab אֹמֶן, a.dy.ac אָמֵן, a.dy.ad אָמָּן, a.dy.ae אֵמֻן, a.dy.af אֱמוּנָה, a.dy.ag אָמְנָה “fostering”, a.dy.ah אָמְנָה “truly”, a.dy.ai אֲמָנָה, a.dy.ak אֻמְנָם, a.dy.al אָמְנָם, a.dy.am אֱמֶת, a.dy.an אָמוֹן “master workman”, xa.as.aa Biblical Aramaic אֲמַן; names in names/: a.dy.ap and a.dy.aq amnon, a.dy.ao amon, a.dy.as heman, a.dy.ar amittai. Left unassigned: a.dy.aj Amana (a river and a mountain: places), a.dy.at מְהוּמָן Mehuman (Est 1:10, a eunuch of Ahasuerus; Wiktionary derives it from Old Persian, though the Peshitta's word for a eunuch is מְהַימְנָא “trusted”, Mat 19:12; Act 8:27: an open question whether the name was heard as Aramaic “trusted”), and the zero-token cross-references a.am.ac, a.ea.an, e.bh.ae, m.ao.ab. Shared tokens: a.dy.an and a.dy.ao each count the 20 tokens of the spelling אָמוֹן: King Amon, Amon of 1Ki 22:26, Amon/Ami of Neh 7:59, the Egyptian god Amun (Jer 46:25; Nah 3:8 נֹא אָמוֹן, Thebes, from Egyptian jmn, TLA tla26060), Pro 8:30 and Jer 52:15. Jer 52:15 הָאָמוֹן is הֶהָמוֹן “the multitude” as in 2Ki 25:11, not this root. The god Amun is a loan from Egyptian and is left out (no Hebrew word; the TIPNR record Amon@Jer.46.25 is not named on the name entry). Psa 12:2; 31:24; Pro 13:17; 14:5; 20:6 are filed both under the verb (no stem) and אֵמֻן; they are entered under אֵמֻן. 2Ki 18:16 הָאֹמְנוֹת is entered as the noun אֹמְנָה with no key. Isa 30:21 is ימנ. Isa 60:4 תֵּאָמַנָה is entered as a niphal passive of the qal “carry”. Job 39:24 is read either “does not stand still” or “does not believe”; both given in one sense. Greek: ἀμήν is a loan (Abbott-Smith); the Septuagint mostly renders אָמֵן by γένοιτο. The Peshitta's words: הימנ (SEDRA root 2034 H;MN: lexemes 165 H;MN believe, 166 H;MNOTA faith, 167 MH;MNA eunuch/faithful, 168 MH;MNA believer), אמנ (root 121 lexeme 162 AM;N amen; root 122 lexemes 163 AM;NA constant, 164 AM;NA;T constantly, 3558 AMN be constant, Col 4:2), and the craft words (root 38 AMN|B: lexemes 47 AOMNA craftsman, 48 AOMNOTA craft). The Peshitta's “truth” is קֻושׁתָּא and “true” שַׁרִירָא, other roots: it does not use this root for אֱמֶת. SEDRA files אוּמָּנָא under a separate root 38 (AMN|B) from the amen words (121, 122). Leads not followed: Ge'ez in Dillmann (cols. for አምነ, ሃይማኖት “faith”, and the loan አሜን) — Anderson–Moser only; Ugaritic (no ʾmn found in Fisher's index; DULAT not consulted); Old South Arabian (ʾmn “security” in Biella not checked); Akkadian CAD for ummiānu and for any ʾmn “firm” (none in the Oracc glossaries; the brief's Akkadian candidates mannu, manû, ummānu are other roots); Payne Smith for the Syriac. Open questions: (1) how the qal “foster, carry” relates to firmness; the noun אָמְנָה and Isa 60:4 hold it together, but no cognate shows it; (2) whether the craftsman words belong to this root or are a loan from Akkadian ummiānu; (3) Pro 8:30 craftsman or nursling; (4) whether הֵימָן (Heman) is from this root; (5) the doctrine statements, especially the-amen and wisdom-beside-yahweh, are reasoned conclusions for the reviewer.
